title: Assemble an aircraft electrical connector
subject: Airframe

sheetSections.name: Insert the Pin into the Electrical Connector

assumptions: The pin type in use has a conductor inspection window.
The pull test is a required acceptance criterion.
Pull-test and continuity results are captured outside the photo submission.
openQuestions: Crimper setup steps (dial, turret, cotter key) are process checks, not artifact checks. If assessment is a single photo of finished work, these are unverifiable after the fact — confirm whether setup is assessed at all.
Reading connector location numbers requires enough resolution and glare-free lighting; this is the small-text case worth testing early in the pilot.

subtasks.label: Prepare the Wire
subtasks.excluded: 1 [document], 1 [measurement] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Select the correct wire gauge for the pin and receiver.

checks.text: The wire gauge used is one the selected pin is rated to accept.

errors.text: Wire gauge outside the pin's compatible range, giving a crimp that cannot develop full strength.

steps.text: Cut the wire to the required length.

checks.text: The cut is square and the conductor strands are not splayed or nicked.

errors.text: Ragged or angled cut leaving splayed strands.

steps.text: Strip 1/8" of insulation off the wire ends.

checks.text: Stripped length is approximately 1/8 inch.
No conductor strands are cut, nicked or missing from the strip operation.

errors.text: Strip too long, leaving bare conductor exposed outside the pin barrel.
Strip too short, so the conductor does not reach the bottom of the barrel.
Nicked or severed strands reducing conductor cross-section.

steps.text: Insert the wire into the pin.

checks.text: The wire seats at the base of the pin opening.
Conductor is visible in the pin's inspection window, confirming full insertion before crimping.

errors.text: Wire bottomed short, so the crimp captures insulation rather than conductor.

sheetPoints.text: Bare stranded conductor is visible at the prepared wire end, insulation removed cleanly.
Bare conductor is inserted into the pin's wire barrel opening.
Insulation ends at or just short of the barrel entry, with no long bare gap.
All strands are gathered inside the barrel; none splayed or standing outside it.
Only one wire enters the pin contact.
Pin barrel is round and free of crimp indentations or tool marks.
The finished work shows no such defect: Pin barrel is empty; the stripped wire lies beside it, uninserted.
The finished work shows no such defect: Insulation is pushed inside the barrel, no bare conductor entering the pin.
The finished work shows no such defect: Strands are visibly cut, broken or fanned outside the barrel mouth.
The finished work shows no such defect: The pin is bent, crushed or split along the barrel.
The finished work shows no such defect: Two wires are inserted into the single pin contact.

steps.text: Open the crimper jaws all the way.

checks.text: Handles are squeezed to release and left resting open before setup.

errors.text: Turret changed with the jaws under load.

steps.text: Insert the crimper turret on the tool face.

checks.text: The turret is keyed into the tool face cut-outs and tangs, seated flat.

errors.text: Turret misaligned on its keying features.

checks.text: Set screws are tightened so the turret cannot shift during crimping.

errors.text: Set screws left loose, allowing turret movement mid-crimp.

steps.text: Turn the handle dial to the wire size being crimped.

checks.text: The handle dial reads the gauge of the wire being crimped.
The cotter key is reinstalled after the selection is made.

errors.text: Dial set to the wrong gauge, giving an under- or over-compressed crimp.
Cotter key left out, allowing the selector to drift.

steps.text: Rotate the turret to the corresponding wire termination size.

checks.text: The correct crimper hole is positioned over the opening and the turret is pressed down until it clicks home.

errors.text: Turret not clicked into detent, leaving the hole misaligned.

checks.text: Handles are squeezed firmly until the tool releases, completing a full cycle.

errors.text: Partial cycle, producing an incomplete crimp.

steps.text: Release the jaws, removing the wire.

checks.text: The termination is withdrawn without deforming the pin.

errors.text: Pin bent or scored on removal.

checks.text: The crimped barrel shows a clean, symmetrical indent with no cracking or splitting.
No bare conductor is exposed between the insulation and the pin barrel.
Pull test: the termination withstands a pull as if pulling it apart and retains the same strength as the wire itself.

errors.text: Termination pulls off or slips under load.

steps.text: Obtain the electrical connector pair and delineate the pin and receiver sides.

checks.text: The pin side is identified as the flat face with craters; the receiver side as the one with wells for the termination.

errors.text: Sides confused, so the termination is installed in the wrong half.

steps.text: Prepare the wire in the installer tool.

checks.text: The wire sits in the installer tool's side channel, pulled taut with the termination contacting the tool.

errors.text: Termination not seated against the tool, so insertion depth is wrong.

steps.text: Install the termination into the correct connector location.

checks.text: The termination is pressed in from the back side until internal resistance is felt, and the tool is withdrawn leaving the wire installed.
The termination occupies the connector location called for by the wiring layout, read against the numbers printed on the connector face.

errors.text: Pin installed in the wrong numbered location.
Installer tool dragged across the rubber insert, damaging the seal that retains the wire.

checks.text: A tug on the wire confirms the termination is seated and locked.
The pin face sits flush and square with the surrounding connector face.

errors.text: Termination backs out under a light pull — not locked.
Pin proud of or recessed below the connector face.

sheetPoints.text: A crimped contact is installed in a contact cavity of the connector
The contact body is seated flush with or below the connector insert face, not standing proud
Only one wire enters the connector at the occupied cavity
The installer tool is clear of the connector, not left in the cavity
Wire insulation is continuous up to the connector rear grommet, no bare conductor showing
The connector insert/grommet around the occupied cavity is intact, no tears or gouges
The finished work shows no such defect: Contact protrudes above the insert face instead of sitting in the cavity.
The finished work shows no such defect: Contact and wire lie loose outside the connector, no contact in any cavity.
The finished work shows no such defect: Pin contact visibly bent, crushed, or its tip broken off.
The finished work shows no such defect: Two wires occupy the same contact cavity.
The finished work shows no such defect: Connector rubber insert visibly torn or gouged at the cavity.
